content.title: Bike Master Plan
content.summary: The Bicycle Master Plan, adopted by Arvada's City Council in October 2017, aims to develop a connected network of low-stress bicycle facilities to promote cycling for transportation and recreation. The plan focuses on creating a safe environment for all cyclists, increasing bicycle access to various destinations, and reducing bicycle-related accidents. An update to the plan is set to begin in 2027, incorporating new design guidance and reflecting progress made over the past decade, with over half of the recommended policies and programs already completed or ongoing.
content.body:
The Bicycle Master Plan was adopted by City Council in October of 2017 and provides the framework to create a connected network of low stress bicycle facilities and support programs that will encourage the untapped potential for bicycling in Arvada, making bicycling for transportation as easy and comfortable as recreational riding. The plan is focused around the following three goals and their objectives:

**Build a connected and comfortable bicycle network by:**

- Increasing the amount of low-stress and state-of-the-art bicycle facilities in Arvada
- Adding north-south bicycle connections and ensuring east-west connections are appropriate
- Increasing perceived comfort of bicyclists and potential bicyclists through encouragement programs

**Create a safe place for all types of bicyclists by:**

- Reducing or eliminating bicycle related crashes, serious injuries, and fatalities
- Focusing on safe crossings of major streets
- Creating a culture of safe bicycling through education and enforcement programs

**Turn bicycling into a convenient form of travel for all trips by:**

- Maximizing bicycle access to a variety of destinations, with a focus on recreational destinations
- Increasing bicycle ridership for all types of trips

## 10-Year Update

The Transportation Planning Team is working towards updating the Bike Master Plan to build on the project and planning work that has occurred over the last ten years. For instance, the Transportation Systems Plan, completed in 2025, provided a renewed prioritization framework for multimodal transportation projects that will be key to informing the Bike Master Plan update.  The update will also focus on incorporating the newest bikeway design guidance and implementation tactics. 

The update is expected to kick off in 2027 and will likely take one to two years between planning, drafting, and adoption. 

## Progress on the 2017 Plan

The plan has three main sections:

1. Programs and policies
2. Bicycle network improvements
3. Olde Town bicycle plan

### Programs and Policies

- 35 education, encouragement, enforcement, and evaluation policies/programs recommended by the plan.
- As of 2025, 54% of the recommended policies and programs are completed or ongoing.
  - Examples include the pursuit of Safe Routes to School funding/projects, starting a counter program on trails, updating the City Code to allow Class 1 and 2 e-bikes, and redesigning Arvada's bike training course.

### Bicycle Network Improvements

- **W 57th, between Independence and Olde Wadsworth:**bike lane and shared markings have been installed
- **Deframe Street:** adding buffered bike lanes
- **Tennyson Street, from W. 58th to W. 64th Ave.:** a current Capital Improvement Project with grant funding that is nearing construction for bike lanes
- **Johnson Street, between each end of Brooks Drive:**this has been established as a bike route with shared pavement markings, we are working on ways to enhance this connection
- **Kipling:** installed a side path
- **Kipling and Oberon Rd between W 69th Pl and 72nd:** installed a shared-use shoulder, with vertical posts for visibility, that connects to sidewalks when present.
- **Alkire between 78th to 80th:** the plan calls for buffered bike lanes; instead, we are installing a side path for greater protection
- **72nd Ave:**installed a side path from Oak to Simms streets
- **86th Parkway:**installing green paint in the bike lane to improve visibility
- **Bike lanes added during repaving:**
  - 62nd Ave between Independence and Garrison
  - Hoyt Way
  - Pomona Dr added buffered bike lanes
  - Vance Dr
  - Yank Way
  - 82nd Ave
  - Club Crest Dr/ Allison Way

### Olde Town Arvada Bicycle Plan

- 14 total program and network/spot improvements recommended by the plan.
- As of 2025, 35% of these programmatic and network/spot improvements have been completed or are ongoing.
  - Examples include the enhancement of Olde Town crosswalks, the installation of parklets and other street interventions in the Olde Town Ped Mall, and a bike parking survey and use count conducted in the Fall of 2025.

## 2016 Community Engagement

The engagement process for developing the Plan occurred in 2016 with an online survey and interactive map, engagement at community events, and partner coordination. Click through the tabs below for more information on what we heard.

1. [How often do you bike for recreation?](#tab34e1ca21-3f1f-447e-97ca-b658c619c3b9_0)

| **Percent of Respondents** | **Response Category** |
| --- | --- |
| **9%** | I do not bike or walk for recreation or exercise |
| **60%** | 1-3 times a week |
| **25%** | 4-5 times a week |
| **6%** | 6+ times a week |

1. [How often do you bike for transportation, such as commuting to work or running errands?](#tab34e1ca21-3f1f-447e-97ca-b658c619c3b9_1)

| **Percent of Respondents** | **Response Category** |
| --- | --- |
| **28%** | I do not bike or walk for transportation |
| **62%** | 1-3 times a week |
| **8%** | 4-5 times a week |
| **2%** | 6+ times a week |

1. [What is the most important to you regarding bicycling access, facilities, and programs?](#tab34e1ca21-3f1f-447e-97ca-b658c619c3b9_2)

- Access to recreation
- Expanding the bicycle network
- Closing gaps between existing bikeways
- More bicycle encouragement programs

1. [What type of bikeway would you feel most comfortable and safe riding within?](#tab34e1ca21-3f1f-447e-97ca-b658c619c3b9_3)

1. Sidepath (32%)
2. Buffered Bike Lane (25%)
3. Protected Bike Lane (24%)

1. [Which of the following strategies is best for building bikeways in Arvada?](#tab34e1ca21-3f1f-447e-97ca-b658c619c3b9_4)

1. Parking Removal (43%)
2. Travel Lane Removal (29%)
3. Road Widening (28%)

1. [Most Desired Routes for Bike Improvements](#tab34e1ca21-3f1f-447e-97ca-b658c619c3b9_5)

- Indiana Street
- Alkire Street
- Kipling Street
- Ward Road

1. [Top Bicycling Destinations](#tab34e1ca21-3f1f-447e-97ca-b658c619c3b9_6)

- Ralston Creek Trail
- Clear Creek Trail
- Five Parks
- Standley Lake
- Community Centers

View the full [Bike Master Plan (PDF)](https://www.arvadaco.gov/DocumentCenter/View/778/2017-Bicycle-Master-Plan-PDF).
